conventions: `לְמָעְלָה` is one unit. The preposition, the adverb and the directive `he` are carried by a single English word, so rules 30 and 32 fuse all three, headed on `מַעַל` — *upward* at 23:27 and *very* at 23:17. Where the Hebrew writes no preposition, as `וָמָעְלָה` at 23:3, the adverb and the `he` fuse alone. Do not mark the `לְ` `unrepresented` beside the adverb: no English word in either verse is spent on it in particular, which is the subtraction test rule 40 runs.

The chapter's multi-level `בַּיִת` chains are written with a *the* before every English noun, and rule 29's count allocates them. Where no article morpheme stands in the chain — `עֲבֹדַת בֵּית יְהוָה` → *the service of the house of Jehovah* (23:24, 23:28, 23:32) — each construct takes a supplied *the*, which rule 29 allows for the second. Where one does — `מַעֲשֵׂה עֲבֹדַת בֵּית הָאֱלֹהִים` → *the work of the service of the house of God* (23:28) — the article's *the* is the one standing before *house*, the word its own noun immediately depends on, and the two outer constructs take supplied *the*s.

The prepositions BSB represents and this chapter leaves `unrepresented` are all recastings that spend no English on the relation, and none is an error to be repaired against BSB: `הָלַל`/`יָדָה` with `לַיהוָה` → *praise Jehovah* (23:5, 23:30) and `נָצַח` with `עַל` → *oversee the work* (23:4), where the object is promoted to a bare direct object; the `לְ` before a bare name in the genealogical list (23:6); the resultative `הָיָה לְ` (23:11) and the possessive `לְ` beside a written `הָיָה` (23:17, 23:22), which takes the *have* itself; the dative `לְ` whose object the ASV makes the English subject of *have need* (23:26); and the prepositions and article of the distributive `בַּבֹּקֶר בַּבֹּקֶר` → *every morning* (23:30), where only the first occurrence is rendered.

promotions.summary: Settles which morpheme owns the *old* of an age written `בֶּן` plus a numeral: the `בֵּן` takes it, the numeral takes its own word, and `שָׁנָה` takes the *years*. Forecloses the two wrong readings a verse pass reaches for — marking `בֵּן` `unrepresented` because no English word writes *son*, and fusing the phrase into one indivisible *years old*.
promotions.basis: Three sites in this chapter (23:3, 23:24, 23:27), all aligned identically and all in the shape `מִבֶּן X שָׁנָה וָמָעְלָה`. The corpus precedent printed for `בֵּן` agrees decisively and contradicts nothing: 104 units align `בֵּן` to *old* headed on *old*, 28 more to *was old*, 10 to *a old* and 5 to *being old*, across 233 chapters, with no unit heading such a phrase on the counted noun and none marking the `בֵּן` unrepresented.
promotions.rule: **An age written with `בֶּן` gives the English *old* to that noun.** Hebrew states an age as `בֶּן` with a numeral, usually with `שָׁנָה` standing after it, and the ASV writes *X years old*: the `בֵּן` takes the *old*, the numeral takes its own word, and `שָׁנָה` takes the *years* as the counted noun, which rule 22 places where a compound numeral distributes it. Do not mark the `בֵּן` `unrepresented` on the ground that no English word writes *son*, and do not fuse the phrase under rule 30: each morpheme has an English word of its own, so rule 2 splits them, and the subtraction test rules 16, 31 and 43 use finds the statement of age gone with the *old* while the numeral and the counted noun are left saying only how many years. The unit is discontinuous under rule 25 wherever the counted noun stands between, which in English is always, since Hebrew writes the `בֵּן` before its numeral and the ASV writes the *old* after the years. The corpus aligns `בֵּן` to *old* in a hundred and four units, to *was old* in twenty-eight, to *a old* in ten and to *being old* in five, and heads every one of them on the word carrying the age, so this is settled rather than a tie to hedge. Three riders. Where the clause is verbless and the ASV writes a copula, that word is the predicate's and joins the `בֵּן` unit under rule 20, which is what those *was old* units are. Where a preposition stands before the `בֵּן` it takes whatever the ASV writes for it under rule 11, as `מִבֶּן עֶשְׂרִים שָׁנָה` → ***from*** *twenty years old* does, and where the ASV leaves that relation unstated the preposition is `unrepresented` under rule 40 as usual. And this governs the age construction only: a `בֵּן` naming a son, and the `בָּנִים` of a bird's young that the ASV writes *young*, are read by the ordinary rules.

report: Read all 48 candidate groups and the dump end to end. No cross-verse split found: every multi-treatment bucket is the ASV rendering one morpheme differently in a context the source licenses.

Age idiom (BEN + numeral + SHANAH) at 23:3, 23:24, 23:27 is identical in all three: BEN takes *old*, the numeral its own word, SHANAH the *years*. That allocation is nowhere in the contract and the corpus agrees (BEN to *old*, 104 units; *was old*, 28), so it is promoted as a new rule.

The two large-unit flags (23:17 unit 19, 23:27 unit 16) are both LE-MAALAH: preposition, adverb and directive he carried by one English word, fused identically in each, *very* in one verse and *upward* in the other. Both atomic.

Article versus supplied *the* is consistent throughout: 23:14 and 23:27 front the phrase's single written *the* onto the present article morpheme, while 23:9, 23:24 and 23:32 write a determiner per noun and give each morpheme the one standing before its own word; 23:28's three-construct chain puts the article's *the* before *house*. All rule 29, decided by counting the ASV's *the*s.
Possessive HAYAH at 23:17 and 23:22 is handled alike: *had* on the written HAYAH, preposition (and in 23:22 the suffix) unrepresented, *no* on the negative recast onto the object nominal.

23:29's seven waws answer one-for-one to seven ASV connectives (also, and, whether, or, or, and, and), so nothing is in surplus and rule 14's correlative pair does not arise. Its articled participle (rule 41, *that which*) beside its articled common noun (rules 29 and 46, *the* on the article and the recasting on the noun) is a source-licensed difference, not a split.

The five `added` runs (said David, therewith, as for, to wife, even) are each supplied English no morpheme licenses; 23:28's *even* goes to its waw because a waw stands there. I re-examined 23:26's *shall no more have need* on the negative existential, the chapter's one place where an arguably surplus word is folded into a morpheme rather than marked `added`; rule 43's reading of the existential keeping the whole frame supports it and the verse note already names the competing reading, so the edge stands.

BSB: all 16 disagreements are documented convention differences (rules 16, 21, 22, 40, 43) — seven prepositions the ASV recasts away, two suffixes left bare beside a written HAYAH or a different construal, the distributive BA-BOQER BA-BOQER, the resumptive HEMMAH, an anarthrously rendered article, and two object markers. No genuine error; no edge changed.
